ChurchStream is free software for **Seventh-day Adventist churches**: live streaming to YouTube and Facebook plus projection of hymns, Bible readings and announcements, from one simple control panel. It runs on Windows and Mac.

## Download

| Computer | Download |
|---|---|
| **Windows** laptop or PC | **[ChurchStream-win-x64.zip](https://github.com/driviere/churchStream/releases/download/v0.4.0/ChurchStream-win-x64.zip)** |
| **Mac with an Apple chip** (M1–M4) | **[ChurchStream-mac-arm64.zip](https://github.com/driviere/churchStream/releases/download/v0.4.0/ChurchStream-mac-arm64.zip)** |
| **Mac with an Intel processor** | **[ChurchStream-mac-x64.zip](https://github.com/driviere/churchStream/releases/download/v0.4.0/ChurchStream-mac-x64.zip)** |

**Updating?** Copy the new files over your old ChurchStream folder; your **ChurchStream-data** folder (settings, songs, services) is kept. First time? See the install steps in the [README](https://github.com/driviere/churchStream#install-windows).

## New in 0.4.0

A bigger update: phones as cameras, a page for a second person to run the stream, the stream on the projector, and video logos.

### A phone as a camera
- Any recent iPhone or Android phone can be **camera 1 or camera 2**, with nothing to install. In **Settings → Camera & sound**, choose **Phone (scan a QR code)** and scan the code with the phone on the **church Wi-Fi**.
- The first time, the phone warns that the connection isn't private. That's expected (the page comes from your own computer): tap **Advanced → Proceed** (Android) or **Show Details → visit this website** (iPhone), then **Start camera**.
- Hold the phone sideways and keep it plugged in. It can switch between front and back cameras and turn on its light.
- If the phone drops off the Wi-Fi, the stream shows "Waiting for the phone camera" instead of freezing, and the picture comes back by itself.
- The sound still comes from your microphone or sound desk. On Windows, allow ChurchStream through the firewall when asked (the camera page uses port 8443).

### A stream page for a second laptop
- A second person can run the live stream from another laptop or tablet while the main computer runs the slides. Open **/stream** on the main computer's address, for example *http://192.168.1.20:8080/stream* (address and QR code in **Settings → Phones & tablets**).
- It has the live picture exactly as viewers see it, the sound meter, YouTube/Facebook status, **Go live / End**, **Camera 1 / Camera 2**, what the stream shows, recording, names, the ticker, and the camera and stream-key settings. Both laptops share the same settings.

### The live stream on the screens
- **Show the live stream on the screens** (under the screen picture) puts the stream on the projector: camera, slides, names and ticker. Handy for an overflow room. It runs about a second behind the room, and starts the camera preview if needed.

### Logo: a picture or a video, up to full screen
- Upload a picture **or a video** as the logo (Settings → General), and choose **Full screen**. A video logo plays silently and repeats while **Logo** is on, on the projector and the stream.

### Change video settings after adding
- Open a video, music or YouTube item to change **Repeat until stopped**, **Also play in the room**, **Volume** and (YouTube) **Start at** at any time. Turning on Repeat while it plays takes effect straight away.

**Also fixed:** a video without a sound track couldn't play into the stream.

**Mac:** replace ChurchStream.app in Applications with the new one. **Windows:** copy the new files over your ChurchStream folder. Your settings and songs in ChurchStream-data are kept.

**Please try a phone at church** before relying on it on Sabbath: the security warning looks a little different on each phone.

## Good to know
- Projecting or streaming hymns still under copyright needs your church's **CCLI** licence (and the Streaming Licence for online use).
- ChurchStream is an independent project, not an official product of the Seventh-day Adventist Church.
